Thinking about Eve in Wasteland’s and getting a better idea of who she is in this dynamic Someone who grew up a Tracker, happy to have the community around them and the support of so many as she grew up with her father and logically also grew up alongside missy. Loses her father due to the conditions of living out in the Tracks, she becomes bitter, growing an internal hatred for the mainlanders and people she deems as privileged, is forced to WORK for said mainlanders to keep her partner from the same fate her father had…. Grows closed off and emotionally distant to what is this close knit community that relies on each other while also becoming a bitter soldier growing more and more discontent towards her mainland coworkers and employers, keeping herself together to not go crazy while she secretly hopes that things change

so like. trying to pinpoint specific jiaolong/jia li inspiration (when it comes to specific media or characters) is difficult because i struggle a little with retaining specific details about how or when i absorbed the kind of information that i used to write them with (beyond deliberate research) but what i can say is that while no specific fictional media comes to mind, they're both inspired off of various people i've seen either in real life or on the internet rather their original non-wastelands character context is that they're inspired by living in richmond BC, which i lived in/adjacent to (Vancouver) while i was going to UBC and the various university students i shared classes with/studied with or lived alongside - richmond BC btw has the highest chinese population in all of north america when it comes to specifically wastelands, a lot of character development happened to specifically fit them for this world while finding organic ways to lace in their earlier character inspirations without feeling out of place i know the inspiration is entirely external because i don't relate to either of them too much but ask me to name any one series or person i will probably die. i don't remember the name of my mandarin language professor (edited)

Some aren’t as familiar with these guys but I am teasing for the inevitable future because I am obsessed with this conversation topic. Joshua: representation of generational mental illness and trauma, and over coming that to not let it define you. How finding your true self (gender/sex) can truly help push you to be the person you were meant to be, and therefore the best version of yourself. I would also call her a representation of true connection in male friendships. Penelope: being your true authentic self even if it means others don’t want you for it. A representation of childish wonder for even the more adult aspects of the world. Olly: a representation of self sacrifice and love. I think he is the pinnacle example of true love in my story. Whether that be platonic or romantic love. He also represents how even kind/GOOD people can be selfish and turn a blind eye.

jiaolong | twa 6/27/2026 4:38 PM
basically 6 is the security type, most fear driven ^^ prioritizing external sources of safety, assurance, stability, protection-seeking i see it in karley via her deference to authority: 6s who believe that the system is there to protect them and others may begin to adopt the system's beliefs, or at least use them as a fall-back 6s struggle with feeling self-trust or like their own internal guidance is sufficient - "if i don't know the answer, then i should listen to the people who do and follow their design, and everything will be okay" thus a 6 of this flavor can be known as well-meaning but rigid and rule-bound; the rules are there for a reason. 5-wing'd 6s tend to have a more introspective quality and patterns of withdrawal whereas a 7-wing's would be pleasure, fun and escapism - 5-wing says when in stress, gather more information and listen as for the tritype i see the heart in 3 - presentation, karley's general insecurity with perception, respect to hierarchy of roles, perfectionism/fear of failure, etc. gut is in 1 - doing it because it's the right way to live, the moral thing to do. code over peace/oblivion, correctness over autonomy/control i say sp/so - i feel like the self-protection instinct kind of takes priority while the social instinct is there but lags behind (as we see Karley kind of struggle with her social bonds/interpretations of people, she processes it a little awkwardly, but still has a social drive/desire in her) - the actual self-protection aspect comes first, and by that i mean the job, the goal, the mission, the important information that comes through first, the thoroughness, physicality, all kind of serve that instinct. That means sx (sexual/one-to-one) is in the blind spot and I kind of feel like that doesn't need so much explaining because Karley does not think about or prioritize making deep chemical bonds with "the one" like that a little bit of a scattered explanation but i hope that helps

It will be updated accordingly as time moves forward. ⇢ THE HISTORY On the planet Aṇḍa, conflicts over resources began to rise which marked the start of The Great Resource War. The world was struck by a series of nuclear weapons causing mass destruction all over. This heavily reduced the population which led to widespread understaffing of nuclear power plants. Most of the land became an irradiated wasteland, and artifacts of the Old World were destroyed.  Recovering the remnants of old civilization became near impossible, however it did not mean that humanity gave up. There were few survivors that prevailed through the disasters located near Saṃśraya. There were safe levels of radiation: an inhabitable space for the human race to start over. Survivors used this spot to create the first Safe Zone, the largest of the two. They would make shelters, ration their food, and gather resources. Many fell victim to what modern society would call "blights"— decaying and distorted animated bodies that refuse to die. This caused a need for more organized efforts to preserve life, thus Luxizor was formed by the wealthy of the Old World. They began to capitalize on necessities, producing items such as gas masks, prosthetics, and medicines in exchange for others' services. This system continued to develop and change with new leadership as years passed on. Soon, Luxizor would manage to be in control of most resources such as food, clothes, and other utilities you could imagine. Laws began to be instated to ensure appropriate usage of resources which would then extend into territories such as social expectations. The modern world as we know it operates under a corpocracy led by the current owner of Luxizor, Jared.
